notes_for_us: Two rules collide head-on here. The intake skill says that when extent and detail cannot both be honoured, offer the decomposition into separate maps — and the prompt pre-emptively forbids exactly that, in its own words, twice. The skill has no third answer, and the honest handoff is a region-band world that will not show a single collectible.

This prompt asks for no combat, and Adventure fits cleanly, which is worth recording as a case where the genre file did its job. The Exploration preset added nothing that was not already in the prompt — the only zero-padding row in this batch.

Movement abilities again: climb, swim, glide and a bicycle all change what counts as traversable ground, and all four ended up as mechanics text. This is the second prompt in this batch where the layout will be validated against the wrong movement model.

notes: A base stacked to fifteen floors overhangs its own footprint, so this is P2 whatever else is picked — and fifteen floors will not read in a single top-down frame. Built as the footprints plus the lower floors, with the upper tiers as a vertical decomposition if the user wants them all visible.
Preset Tycoon kept; its plot-shared shape was replaced with plot-isolated because the prompt says a base for each player.

The prompt is loosely worded and partly ambiguous — 'objetivos' next to 'objetos', and it is not clear whether the parking is for vehicles or is where objects are collected. Built the reading that the street spawns objects and the bases store them.

notes_for_us: 'Floor 15' is the third number in this batch that only survives as free text. Counts attach to options, and this one belongs to the shape — a per-player plot that grows vertically to a stated height — so there is nowhere for it to go.

The skill tells you to ask about a term you genuinely cannot parse, and that is the right instruction, but on a prompt this loose it would take three or four such questions and the ceiling is four in total. The cap is written for prompts that are clear except in one place.
No option covers a parking bay, and parking is a common Roblox ask — car dealerships, delivery jobs, street games all want marked stalls to leave a vehicle in.
